principle: Research results become product hypotheses, not automatic feature decisions.

evidence_levels.established: Supported by a review, meta-analysis, or repeated research.
evidence_levels.strong_signal: Useful experimental or field evidence, but context still matters.
evidence_levels.emerging: Recent evidence that needs more replication.

studies.finding: People often move information into external tools to reduce the amount they must keep active in their mind.
studies.product_hypothesis: Capture should be extremely fast. Structure can come later. Wooolfmesh should remember commitments, context, and next steps so the user does not have to keep rehearsing them mentally.
studies.test: Test a one-action capture inbox with later clarification and a visible confirmation that the item is safely stored.
studies.citation: Risko, E. F., & Gilbert, S. J. (2016). Cognitive Offloading.

studies.finding: When people leave unfinished work, part of their attention can stay with the previous task and reduce performance on the next task.
studies.product_hypothesis: Focus should protect the active task while making interruptions safe to capture without opening a new work stream.
studies.test: Keep interruption capture inside Focus and close a session with outcome, next action, and an exact resume point.
studies.citation: Leroy, S. (2009). Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks.

studies.finding: If-then plans can help people translate goals into action by connecting a situation with a planned response.
studies.product_hypothesis: Routines can be more useful when they are linked to clear triggers instead of only fixed schedules.
studies.test: Test local trigger rules such as: if a focus session ends with an open blocker, propose it for tomorrow's review. Durable changes stay preview-first.
studies.citation: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes.

studies.finding: Trying to recall information can improve later retention more than simply reading the same material again.
studies.product_hypothesis: Cognitive bites should sometimes help the user retrieve a lesson, not only display it.
studies.test: Test an optional Recall first card for important lessons, decisions, and mistakes linked to current work.
studies.citation: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. (2006). Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention.

studies.finding: A CHI 2025 study found that higher confidence in generative AI was linked with less reported critical-thinking effort. Critical thinking also moved toward verification, integration, and supervision.
studies.product_hypothesis: AI should make verification easy and keep the user responsible for important decisions instead of only producing polished answers.
studies.test: Show sources, confidence, assumptions, and verify-before-apply cues for higher-impact AI suggestions.
studies.citation: Lee et al. (2025). The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers.

studies.finding: A CHI 2025 experiment found different cognitive patterns when AI led a task, co-led it, or was absent. More automation was not simply better in every dimension.
studies.product_hypothesis: Some workflows may work better when AI gives one step, question, or suggestion at a time instead of one complete answer.
studies.test: Test a co-led task shaping mode that asks one useful question before generating a full plan.
studies.citation: Productive vs. Reflective: How Different Ways of Integrating AI into Design Workflows Affect Cognition and Motivation (CHI 2025).

studies.finding: A CHI 2025 study of daily-assistant agents found that plan quality and user involvement both matter. Plausible-looking plans can still create misplaced trust.
studies.product_hypothesis: Agent work should be inspectable before execution, with bounded steps and visible checkpoints.
studies.test: Use Plan -> Preview -> Approve -> Execute for agent workflows and keep a local action log.
studies.citation: Plan-Then-Execute: An Empirical Study of User Trust and Team Performance When Using LLM Agents As Daily Assistants (CHI 2025).

studies.finding: A 2026 productivity-agent study found lower workload with agentic support, while medium autonomy gave the best balance between productivity and preference for control in that study.
studies.product_hypothesis: The useful choice may not be manual versus fully autonomous. Different actions can have different autonomy levels based on risk and user choice.
studies.test: Allow pre-approved low-risk local actions while keeping durable or destructive actions behind explicit confirmation.
studies.citation: Geninatti Cossatin et al. (2026). The autonomy equation: How agentic AI reshapes trust and workload in routine productivity applications.
